## Funding the infrastructure behind AI

[Marlon Nichols](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marloncnichols/) , managing partner at MaC Venture Capital, compares the moment to earlier infrastructure booms.
“Every technology cycle mints a small group of companies that sell what everyone else ends up depending on, like AWS in the Cloud era and Cisco during the internet boom. Agents are the next cycle… none of that happens until enterprises can put real weight behind them and trust them with decisions that matter,” he said.

The $3.6 million in FriskAI’s total funding to date will go toward expanding its engineering and go-to-market teams. Whether it’s enough to build that trust before Geordie or Oasis lock down the same customers is a different question entirely.

FriskAI has emerged from stealth with the launch of its runtime intelligence platform for artificial intelligence agents and a $3.6 million pre-seed funding round aimed at supporting its expansion. The financing was led by MaC Venture Capital, with participation from Wischoff Ventures, NEA partner Rick Yang, and a group of strategic angel investors. Because these systems can behave differently depending on the circumstances they encounter, enterprises may face new security, compliance, governance, and reliability concerns that conventional observability platforms were not specifically designed to address. ## Focus on Regulated Industries

FriskAI is initially positioning its technology for organizations operating in high-stakes sectors such as healthcare, insurance, and financial services, where understanding automated activity can be particularly important for regulatory and operational oversight.

He argued that enterprises will need infrastructure capable of helping them see what autonomous systems are doing, protect the resources those systems interact with, and establish sufficient trust before assigning them more important responsibilities. * * *

FriskAI is launching at a time when enterprises are increasingly exploring autonomous AI systems while confronting questions about how those systems can be monitored, governed, and secured in production. By creating a dedicated runtime intelligence layer, the company is seeking to give organizations greater insight into agent decisions and activities as AI becomes more deeply integrated into critical business workflows.
With fresh funding and backing from venture investors, FriskAI is betting that visibility into AI agent behavior will become an essential component of enterprise infrastructure as organizations scale autonomous technologies.

The company's platform sits around agent runtimes, capturing detailed traces of each action an autonomous system takes in production: which tools it calls, what arguments it passes, what it returns, how long operations take. Teams don't set thresholds or write detection rules themselves; the system learns normal behavior and surfaces anomalies automatically.
